stem:
Aryan builds a growing triangle pattern with toothpicks. Shape $1$ uses $3$ toothpicks, Shape $2$ uses $5$ toothpicks, and Shape $3$ uses $7$ toothpicks.

Which countable feature produces the related number sequence $3$, $5$, $7$, $\ldots$?

options.text: Count the toothpicks in Shape $1$ only, then reuse that same count for every later shape.
Count every interior angle in any polygon from the chapter, as if that also made this sequence.
Count the toothpicks that make up each whole shape; repeating that same count gives $3$, $5$, $7$, $\ldots$.
Pick the printed numeral $7$ alone because it is the largest number shown.

teacher.key_rationale: The related sequence comes from counting the same structural feature—toothpicks—in each whole figure. Counting only Shape 1, counting angles from elsewhere, or grabbing the printed 7 miss that hinge.
